summary: Interpreted the shutdown-race receipt and corrected my first reading of it: outcomes labelled 'violated' for the verify case mean one evaluated trial contradicted the assertion, not all of them, and the underlying events show the predicted hang in two of three trials — 9 and 41 of 64 VerifyLeader futures were still uncompleted 400ms after Shutdown() returned, against 0 of 64 in the no-shutdown control, while every completed call returned success. The mechanism is now described from source: the request sits in the buffered verifyCh (64 slots) that the exiting run loop never drains, and the verifyFuture's ShutdownCh is never set, so Error() has nothing to unblock on; the contract names ErrRaftShutdown as a possible error and the repository's own test file carries a TODO for this class. Barrier and Apply left no future incomplete in the same run (0 of 192 each), which fits applyCh being drained in batches while verifyCh is drained one case per iteration, so the exposure is timing dependent and the third trial's zero is recorded as counterevidence rather than smoothed over. A Fact records the observation with its indices; no execution requested this turn. Unfinished: bounding how long a stranded future stays unanswerable and contrasting racing calls with post-shutdown calls that do return ErrRaftShutdown.
